note: Random encounter dialogue (src/ai/encounters.gd): eighteen kinds. Original writing.

lines.speaker: wagoner
lines.line: Wheel's off the axle and my back's not what it was in the war. Don't suppose you'd lend a shoulder?

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Hold the team steady. On three.

lines.speaker: wagoner
lines.line: Bless you. Here, take this. Flour's spoiled but the coffee ain't.

lines.speaker: bandit
lines.line: That's far enough. Purse, pistol and the horse, in that order, and nobody's widow-making today.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Already a widow. You'll have to do better than that.

lines.speaker: prisoner
lines.line: Ma'am! Ma'am, this boy's taking me to hang for a horse I paid for. Cut me loose and I'll make it worth your while.

lines.speaker: deputy
lines.line: Don't you listen to him. Ride on, ma'am. This is county business.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: County business. Then I'll leave it to the county.

lines.speaker: snakebit
lines.line: Rattler got me through the boot. Leg's going numb. You carry anything for it?

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Sit down and stop walking on it. This'll taste like a tannery.

lines.speaker: snakebit
lines.line: Owe you my leg and likely the rest of me. There's a creek past the mesa where the color shows. Go look.

lines.speaker: hunter
lines.line: Venison, fresh this morning. Four bits a quarter. Cheaper than shooting it yourself and twice as quiet.

lines.speaker: widow
lines.line: He wanted to be buried where he could see the river. Couldn't dig it deep enough. Ground's like iron.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Give me the shovel. Sit a while.

lines.speaker: agent
lines.line: Now, boys! Before she reaches the wash!

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Rocks on the left. Three of them, and none of them can count to cover.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: They waited all morning in the sun for whatever's in my saddlebags. It's mostly coffee.

lines.speaker: condemned
lines.line: I never touched their stock! Ma'am, I bought that steer at Greer's with a bill of sale, and they burned it!

lines.speaker: captain
lines.line: Keep riding, ma'am. This is the Vigilance Committee's business, and we've a rope's worth of it left.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Cut him down. If he stole, there's a judge in Bitter Spring who'd like the work.

lines.speaker: captain
lines.line: You're Caddell. I've heard what you did for the Halvorsens. All right. He goes to the sheriff, and if he's lying, he hangs anyhow.

lines.speaker: captain
lines.line: I don't know you, and I don't care to. Boys, she wants to share his limb.

lines.speaker: condemned
lines.line: I'll never forget it, ma'am. Not a day. I'm going to name a child after you, and I'm not even married.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Not my rope. Not my business. I'll tell myself that till Sunday, I expect.

lines.speaker: farmwife
lines.line: Help! The team's bolted! Somebody stop them!

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Whoa, whoa now. Easy. Easy. They're only frightened, ma'am. So are you. So am I.

lines.speaker: farmwife
lines.line: A jackrabbit. A jackrabbit, and eleven hundred pounds of horse went out of its mind. My husband will never believe you.

lines.speaker: farmwife
lines.line: My arm. I think it's broke. Don't mind me. The flour, though. Thirty pounds of flour all over the county.

lines.speaker: lostgirl
lines.line: I followed a jackrabbit and then the house went away. Mama says never follow a jackrabbit. I forgot.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Houses don't go away. They just hide behind hills. Take my hand and we'll find yours.

lines.speaker: lostgirl
lines.line: Do you have a little girl? You've got a sad face. Mama has a sad face too when Papa's late.

lines.speaker: mother
lines.line: Lord, Lord. I've been calling three hours. Here, take this. It isn't much. Please, take it.

lines.speaker: tolliver
lines.line: You're Ruth Caddell. They say you're quick. I say they never saw me. Twenty paces, or are the stories made up?

lines.speaker: tolliver
lines.line: Ruth Caddell. Every saloon from here to Coldwater says you're a killer. Let's see if you can do it with somebody looking at you.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Twenty paces, then. When you're ready, son. I won't go first.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Nineteen, maybe. Somebody gave him that gun belt for his birthday.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Go home, son. The stories are true, and none of them end the way you'd want. Sell that belt and buy your mother a stove.

lines.speaker: tolliver
lines.line: I hate you for this. I expect I'll be glad of it later. Don't tell anybody I walked away.

lines.speaker: seller
lines.line: Professor Whitlow's Mountain Balsam! Cures the rheumatism, the catarrh, the weak blood and the poor attitude. Two dollars, and it's cheap at four.

lines.speaker: seller
lines.line: A woman of judgment! Two spoons at bedtime. Three if the bedtime is lonesome.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: It smells like grain spirit and pepper. Well. That'll cure somebody of something.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Folks, it's rye whiskey and red pepper in a pretty bottle. You can get both at Greer's for a quarter.

lines.speaker: seller
lines.line: Madam, you have ruined an honest swindle. I hope your rheumatism is particularly rheumatic.

lines.speaker: coyle
lines.line: Ruth Caddell. Your face is on a poster, and the poster is on a fence, and the fence is worth money to me. Let's make this easy.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Here's the county's money. Carry it in and tell them it's settled. You'll get your cut of nothing.

lines.speaker: coyle
lines.line: A fair trade. I don't like shooting women, and I like being shot by them even less.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: That poster's paper Pell paid for. You're riding for the syndicate and you don't even get a badge.

lines.speaker: coyle
lines.line: Paper's paper. Pays the same whoever printed it.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: If you want it, come and collect it. I'll stand right here.

lines.speaker: traveller
lines.line: Mare threw a shoe and then threw me. I've walked twelve miles on a dry canteen. You wouldn't have a swallow?

lines.speaker: traveller
lines.line: That's kind. Truly. Now the purse, slow, and don't make me sorry I asked nicely the first time.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Next time somebody asks me for water, I'll pour it on the ground in front of him and watch.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: He should have asked for the horse. I might have given him the horse.

lines.speaker: drunk
lines.line: Lady! Lady! Have a pull and shoot a bottle with me! I've been drunk since Tuesday, and I'm winning!

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: One pull. Then you sleep it off under that tree, and the bottles live to fight another day.

lines.speaker: drunk
lines.line: You're a Christian woman. A Christian woman with a terrible thirst. I like you.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Hand me the pistol, grip first. You can have it back in Bitter Spring when you can spell it.

lines.speaker: drunk
lines.line: My granddaddy carried that at Shiloh. He never hit anything either.

lines.speaker: homesteader
lines.line: The barn! The barn's caught! There's buckets by the trough, for the love of God, take one!

lines.speaker: homesteader
lines.line: Black on one side and standing. Lord. I'd have lost the hay and the mules. You'll eat with us. Don't argue.

lines.speaker: homesteader
lines.line: It's gone. The house stood, though. A barn's only lumber, my wife says. My wife is a better Christian than I am.

lines.speaker: preacher
lines.line: Sister, I'm raising a church at Windmill Flats one board at a time. A dollar's two boards and a nail.

lines.speaker: preacher
lines.line: I know your name, sister. I've heard it from pulpits, and not kindly. Even so, the church needs boards, and the Lord takes all kinds of money.

lines.speaker: preacher
lines.line: I'll write your name on a board. On the inside, if you'd rather. The Lord reads both sides.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Build it with somebody else's boards, Reverend. I'll come to the first funeral.

lines.speaker: preacher
lines.line: That's what they all say. I've never lacked for funerals.

lines.speaker: agent
lines.line: Keep riding, lady. This ain't your coach and it ain't your business.

lines.speaker: driver
lines.line: Twenty years on the box and never been robbed till today, and never been saved neither. The company'll hear of this. Here, from the strongbox.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Not my coach. I'll be hearing that woman cry all the way to the river.
